Data and sources (14)

14 displayed observations: 9 PL R&D text-equivalent estimates included in the fit; 5 context marks excluded (2 paper-reported native task rates, 1 company native task rate and 2 unresolved image estimates).

PL R&D text-equivalent estimates use an equiprobable 28-symbol modeling alphabet: 26 letters, a space and one extra symbol are our declared choice, not the actual task keyboard. log2(28) ≈ 4.8 assumed bits/character is an ideal finite-codebook equivalent, not measured English entropy or 8-bit storage (a literal fixed-width 28-symbol code needs 5 bits). Speech assumes five characters per word, including spaces: a normalization convention, not measured corpus word length. CPM × log2(28)/60; WPM × 5 × log2(28)/60. Calculations use full precision.

No extra WER/CER penalty: native correct-character rates already include correction time; the gross pace of speech and handwriting keeps reported errors separate. Vansteensel uses the reported 33 seconds/letter timing, not native correct CPM. Assistance and tasks differ: dictionary disambiguation, prediction, completion and language models can contribute to output. Correlations and language-model output mean these are not measured neural information rates, error-standardized results or a common performance benchmark.

Only 9 text-equivalent observations enter the fit; 5 context marks are excluded: 3 native task/company bits/s rates (unchanged) and 2 unresolved image estimates. All 14 marks retain reference-year placement. Bacher uses the 2015 issue (online 2014); Stentrode the 2021 issue (online 2020); home speech the 2025 preprint (final paper 2026). Named Bacher, Vansteensel and Milekovic/Sarma results are selections for our chart, not recovered original-dot assignments. Original image coordinates and historical candidate leads remain archived.

Equal-weight ordinary least squares of log10(text-equivalent bits/s) against reference year across 9 converted-text observations; 5 context marks are excluded (3 native task-bps, 2 unresolved image estimates). log10(rate) = -0.587690 + 0.216845 × (year − 2015); R² in log10 space = 0.846969. Descriptive subset fit over 2015–2025 only; assistance, error metrics and tasks differ. Not a common performance benchmark, measured neural ITR, causal growth estimate or forecast. No confidence band is shown.

Kennedy & BakayCursor / grid control	2000 · reference-year placement; source date below	≈0.24	Identified report; numerical value unresolved: Direct control of a computer from the human central nervous system ↗
Our present patient has learned to control the cursor for the production of synthetic speech and typing.

Image estimate. Reported input: Approximately 0.24 bits/s from the reference image; native numeric result unresolved. Image digitization only; no text conversion or verified source-native rate. Reference image: approximately 0.24 bits/s; original image coordinates remain archived separately. Publication/disclosure: 2000 (paper publication year). The paper is identified at metadata/abstract level; its full numerical result is unverified. No typing-rate conversion is used for this dot. Context; excluded from fit.


Cursor control A · source unconfirmedCursor / grid control	2015 · reference-year placement; source date below	≈0.9	Anonymous reference-image mark · assignment unresolved
Cursor / Grid control

Image estimate. Approximately 0.9 bits/s, digitized from the reference. The papers below are plausible candidates, not confirmed assignments; this dot has not been replaced by a converted candidate result. Context; excluded from fit.

Candidate sources · assignment unconfirmed

Possible Gilja et al. 2015 · moderate confidence ↗

Supplementary Table 1 prints 0.93 and 0.92 Fitts bits/s, excluding hold time. Year and rate are plausible, but this is not achieved-grid bitrate and no original chart data confirms the assignment. Jarosiewicz is an equally plausible alternative.

Possible Jarosiewicz et al. 2015 · alternative ↗

The original paper defines radial-keyboard extrapolated bitrate. Pandarinath 2017 Table 1 later reports T6 0.93 bits/s (four-person average 0.59). That retrospective result is compatible with this mark but does not identify it.


Bacher et al.Text selection / scanning	2015 · reference-year placement; source date below	≈0.753	Reported input: Neural point-and-click communication by a person with incomplete locked-in syndrome ↗
In the “keyboard” task, the number of keystrokes per minute (QWERTY: 7.1 ± 1.7, Radial: 12.3 ± 1.1 kspm, p < 0.001) and the number of correct characters per minute (QWERTY: 5.7 ± 2.0, Radial: 9.4 ± 3.2 ccpm, p = 0.019) were higher using the Radial Keyboard compared to the QWERTY keyboard.

PL R&D estimate. Reported input: 9.4 ± 3.2 correct characters/minute; radial ‘keyboard ’ condition, completion off; ambiguous-key disambiguation retained (not the 10.4-CPM completion condition). 9.4 correct characters/minute × log2(28) bits/character ÷ 60. No extra error penalty: correct CPM already accounts for correction. Completion is off; ambiguous-key disambiguation remains. Reference image: approximately 0.76 bits/s; original image coordinates remain archived separately. Publication/disclosure: 2014-11-10 (first online publication; 2015 journal issue). Explicitly selected paper-backed observation for this chart, not a confirmed assignment of the original author's dot. Text-equivalent; fit included.


Vansteensel et al.Text selection / scanning	2016 · reference-year placement; source date below	≈0.146	Reported input: Fully Implanted Brain–Computer Interface in a Locked-In Patient with ALS ↗
Spelling initially took 52 seconds per letter; the time required dropped to 33 seconds per letter when word prediction was used.

PL R&D estimate. Reported input: 33 seconds/letter with prediction assistance (= 60/33 characters/minute), rather than the rounded two letters/minute summary. (60/33) characters/minute × log2(28) bits/character ÷ 60 = log2(28)/33 bits/s. Gross output pace with prediction assistance. No error penalty; no extra WER/CER factor. Reference image: approximately 0.16 bits/s; original image coordinates remain archived separately. Publication/disclosure: 2016-11-12 (first online publication). Explicitly selected paper-backed observation for this chart, not a confirmed assignment of the original author's dot. Text-equivalent; fit included.


Milekovic / Sarma et al.Text selection / scanning	2018 · reference-year placement; source date below	≈0.551	Reported input: Stable long-term BCI-enabled communication in ALS and locked-in syndrome using LFP signals ↗
The average spelling performance, as measured by the number of correct characters per minute (CCPM), during free-spelling blocks using word completion was 3.07 ± 0.20 CCPM and 6.88 ± 0.33 CCPM for T2 and T6, respectively.

PL R&D estimate. Reported input: 6.88 ± 0.33 correct characters/minute, T6 free spelling with word completion using FlashSpeller neural-switch scanning. 6.88 correct characters/minute × log2(28) bits/character ÷ 60. No extra error penalty: correct CPM already accounts for correction. Word completion remains part of the task. Reference image: approximately 0.53 bits/s; original image coordinates remain archived separately. Publication/disclosure: 2018-04-25 (first online publication). Explicitly selected paper-backed observation for this chart, not a confirmed assignment of the original author's dot. Text-equivalent; fit included.


Pandarinath et al.Cursor / grid control	2017 · reference-year placement; source date below	4.16	Paper-reported: High performance communication by people with paralysis using an intracortical brain-computer interface ↗
average performance was 4.16 ± 0.39 bps

Paper-reported. Reported input: 4.16 ± 0.39 bits/s, T5 9×9 grid; mean across eight blocks/two days. Native task bits/s retained as reported; not converted using the text convention. Reference image: approximately 3.5 bits/s; original image coordinates remain archived separately. Publication/disclosure: 2017-02-21 (paper publication). The paper also reports 3.7 ± 0.4 bits/s for T5 on a 6×6 grid. The chart explicitly selects the 9×9 mean, not the single 4.36-bits/s example block; the original figure's exact choice is unknown. Context; excluded from fit.


Neuralink PRIMECursor / grid control	2024 · reference-year placement; source date below	8	Company-reported: PRIME Study Progress Update — User Experience (company report) ↗
He has subsequently achieved 8.0 BPS and is currently trying to beat scores of the Neuralink engineers using a mouse (~10 BPS).

Company-reported. Reported input: 8.0 bits/s achieved Webgrid performance, Neuralink's May 8, 2024 update; not a peer-reviewed paper. Native task bits/s retained as reported; not converted using the text convention. Reference image: approximately 8.7 bits/s; original image coordinates remain archived separately. Publication/disclosure: 2024-05-08 (company disclosure). This is a company disclosure, not independent validation. The original figure's exact value/date/grid pairing is unknown. Context; excluded from fit.


Synchron StentrodeEndovascular switch	2021 · reference-year placement; source date below	≈0.46	Paper-reported estimate: Motor neuroprosthesis implanted with neurointerventional surgery improves capacity for activities of daily living tasks in severe paralysis ↗
The participant achieved 1.33 (1.58, 0.94–1.58) bits/trial at an ITR of 0.46 (0.41, 0.28–0.63) bits s -1 with the motor neuroprosthesis alone, and 4.43 (4.95, 3.85–4.95) bits/trial at an ITR of 1.57 (1.40, 0.98–2.11) bits s -1 was transmitted with the motor neuroprosthesis + eye-tracker.

Paper-reported estimate. Reported input: 0.46 bits/s, participant 2 mean estimated isolated motor-neuroprosthesis contribution. Actual typing also used eye tracking; this is the authors' isolated-contribution estimate, not the hybrid 1.57-bits/s result. Native task bits/s retained as reported; not converted using the text convention. Reference image: approximately 0.47 bits/s; original image coordinates remain archived separately. Publication/disclosure: 2020-10-28 (online publication; February 2021 journal issue). The isolated contribution is an author estimate; actual typing used eye tracking. Participant 1's isolated estimate was 0.32 bits/s. Context; excluded from fit.


Willett et al. · handwritingHandwriting decoding	2021 · reference-year placement; source date below	≈7.21	Reported input: High-performance brain-to-text communication via handwriting ↗
Notably, typing speeds were high, plateauing at 90 characters per minute with a mean character error rate of 5.4% (averaged across all four blocks on the final day) (Fig. 2c).

PL R&D estimate. Reported input: 90 characters/minute with 5.4% character error rate on the final evaluation day, from Willett et al. 2021. 90 characters/minute × log2(28) bits/character ÷ 60. PL R&D code-equivalent estimate of gross decoding pace, not measured neural ITR. No error penalty; 5.4% CER remains separate. Reference image: approximately 6.6 bits/s; original image coordinates remain archived separately. Publication/disclosure: 2021-05-12 (first online publication; issue 2021-05-13). The final-day 5.4% character error rate is distinct from the overall five-day 94.1% accuracy. The selected 90-CPM gross pace is converted by PL R&D without a CER penalty; no author corrected-typing model is used. Text-equivalent; fit included.


Moses & ChangSpeech decoding	2021 · reference-year placement; source date below	≈6.09	Reported input: Neuroprosthesis for Decoding Speech in a Paralyzed Person with Anarthria ↗
We decoded sentences from the participant’s cortical activity in real time at a median rate of 15.2 words per minute, with a median word error rate of 25.6%.

PL R&D estimate. Reported input: 15.2 words/minute; real-time visually prompted sentence decoding, language model enabled. 25.6% word error rate. 15.2 words/minute × 5 assumed characters/word × log2(28) bits/character ÷ 60. PL R&D code-equivalent estimate of gross decoding pace, not measured neural ITR. No error penalty; the reported error metric remains separate. Reference image: approximately 1.2 bits/s; original image coordinates remain archived separately. Publication/disclosure: 2021-07-14 (first online publication; issue 2021-07-15). Prompted sentences with a language model and a restricted 50-word vocabulary. WPM and WER are source-level medians with different aggregation, not a per-trial channel estimate. Text-equivalent; fit included.


Willett et al. · speechSpeech decoding	2023 · reference-year placement; source date below	≈24.8	Reported input: A high-performance speech neuroprosthesis ↗
T12 achieved a 9.1% word error rate for the 50-word vocabulary across all vocalizing days (11.2% for silent) and a 23.8% word error rate for the 125,000-word vocabulary across all vocalizing days (24.7% for silent).

PL R&D estimate. Reported input: 62 words/minute; real-time held-out prompted sentences. 23.8% word error rate. 62 words/minute × 5 assumed characters/word × log2(28) bits/character ÷ 60. PL R&D code-equivalent estimate of gross decoding pace, not measured neural ITR. No error penalty; the reported error metric remains separate. Reference image: approximately 4.9 bits/s; original image coordinates remain archived separately. Publication/disclosure: 2023-08-23 (first online publication). The 23.8% WER applies to the 125,000-word vocalized condition; the paper's 9.1% WER belongs to a separate 50-word condition. Evaluation used held-out prompted sentences, not free conversation. Text-equivalent; fit included.


Metzger & ChangSpeech decoding	2023 · reference-year placement; source date below	≈31.4	Reported input: A high-performance neuroprosthesis for speech decoding and avatar control ↗
We observed a median real-time decoding rate of 78.3 WPM (99% CI \[75.5, 79.4\]; Fig. 2f).

PL R&D estimate. Reported input: 78.3 words/minute; real-time text decoding of held-out silently attempted prompted sentences. 25.5% word error rate. 78.3 words/minute × 5 assumed characters/word × log2(28) bits/character ÷ 60. PL R&D code-equivalent estimate of gross decoding pace, not measured neural ITR. No error penalty; the reported error metric remains separate. Reference image: approximately 6.2 bits/s; original image coordinates remain archived separately. Publication/disclosure: 2023-08-23 (first online publication). Online evaluation used 1,024 words. The 39,378-word condition was an offline simulation; a later anatomical correction did not change real-time decoding performance. Text-equivalent; fit included.


Card & StaviskySpeech decoding	2024 · reference-year placement; source date below	≈12.7	Reported input: An Accurate and Rapidly Calibrating Speech Neuroprosthesis ↗
The mean decoding performance for the copy task in the final five evaluation sessions was a word error rate of 2.5% (95% CI, 2.0 to 3.1) at the participant’s self-paced speaking rate of 31.6 words per minute (95% CI, 31.2 to 32.0) (Fig. S1B), with individual daily mean word error rates ranging from 1.0 to 3.3% (Table S3).

PL R&D estimate. Reported input: 31.6 words/minute; prompted copy task at self-paced speaking rate. 2.5% word error rate. 31.6 words/minute × 5 assumed characters/word × log2(28) bits/character ÷ 60. PL R&D code-equivalent estimate of gross decoding pace, not measured neural ITR. No error penalty; the reported error metric remains separate. Reference image: approximately 2.6 bits/s; original image coordinates remain archived separately. Publication/disclosure: 2024-08-14 (first online publication; issue 2024-08-15). 31.6 WPM and 2.5% WER are the final five copy-task session means. The reference figure's 33-WPM label is a different, unverified selection. Text-equivalent; fit included.


Card & Stavisky · home useSpeech decoding	2025 · reference-year placement; source date below	≈22.5	Reported input: Long-term independent use of an intracortical brain-computer interface for speech and cursor control ↗
He communicated 183,060 sentences – totaling 1,960,163 words – at an average rate of 56.1 words per minute.

PL R&D estimate. Reported input: 56.1 words/minute; unconstrained personal use at home. 56.1 words/minute × 5 assumed characters/word × log2(28) bits/character ÷ 60. PL R&D code-equivalent estimate of gross decoding pace, not measured neural ITR. No error penalty; the reported error metric remains separate. Reference image: approximately 4.4 bits/s; original image coordinates remain archived separately. Publication/disclosure: 2025-07-07 (bioRxiv v1 posting, not DOI date string; peer-reviewed online publication 2026-06-15). Personal home use has no paired WER here. The 99.2% copy-task accuracy and 92.3% participant-rated sentence correctness are different endpoints. This follows the same participant as Card 2024, not an independent cohort. Text-equivalent; fit included.
